_comment: csm-cascade-selection-verification (B.86b): dedicated scene for CSM's golden-reference cascade-selection check ('csmCascadeIndex' capture). A long receding floor plane under a shallow-angle camera puts view-space depth in [~0.5, ~64] across the frame, spanning CSM's compile-time default 4-cascade PSSM(lambda=0.75) split boundaries for this camera's near=0.5/far=60 (computed via CSMSplitMath::computeCascadeSplitDistance at bless time: cascade0 far ~7.6, cascade1 far ~16.7, cascade2 far ~32.3, cascade3 far=60) -- crossing all three internal boundaries, well past the 'at least two' requirement. This scene relies on CSM's settings staying at their compile-time defaults (numCascades=4, PSSM, lambda=0.75, shadowMaxDistance=0) since no scene-JSON mechanism pins them; a future default change silently invalidates the golden reference (see design.md Risks). Unlike AO's golden scene, the directional light here MUST have castShadows:true -- Scene::getPrimaryDirectionalLight() filters on enabled && castShadows, and CSM's directionalActive gate (which the new capture pass's declaration depends on) is exactly that pointer being non-null. The floor object itself still sets castsShadows:false; it's the receiver under test, not a caster.
